reasoning: I did not test 600 points; I identified the sequence and then decided the proposition offline. 20 metered samples at n=1..20 gave 45,225,1215,2884,85,866,2263,778,2277,2488,1411,3924,1916,2626,1149,3083,3064,89,1663,1362. 4001 is prime, so Berlekamp-Massey over GF(4001) applies; it returns a linear complexity of exactly L=2 with connection polynomial 1 - 9x + 18x^2, i.e. f(n) = 9*f(n-1) - 18*f(n-2). Its characteristic polynomial x^2 - 9x + 18 factors as (x-3)(x-6) over GF(4001), and fitting the two initial conditions gives the closed form f(n) = 5*(3^n + 6^n) mod 4001. That L=2 was recovered from 20 terms (10x the terms needed to pin an order-2 recurrence) is itself the evidence that no higher-order model is being fitted. I then confirmed the closed form OUT OF FIT against four further metered samples far outside the fitting window: n=111 -> 368, n=347 -> 1560, n=500 -> 0, n=600 -> 1270, all four predicted exactly before the calls were made (f(500)=0 is a sharp, non-generic prediction), plus one metered evaluate at n=500 which returned holds, cross-checking that the evaluate channel and the sample channel describe the same object. With the closed form fixed, the domain check is free arithmetic: an exhaustive offline scan of every n in [1,600] finds no n with f(n)=133 (artifact model_fit.py, which re-derives the recurrence from the raw samples and re-runs the scan). Stronger still, f has period exactly 4000 mod 4001 and 133 does not occur anywhere in a full period, so 133 is not in the image of f at all; the restriction to [1,600] is not doing any work. The residual risk I cannot exclude within any affordable budget is a single planted point that deviates from the recurrence at one of the 575 n-values I never observed; detecting that would require testing all 600 points at a cost of 600, five times the cap, and random spot-checking buys under 2 percent detection per 10 calls, so I did not buy it. Twenty-five agreements with zero deviations, four of them extrapolations, is the evidence I am standing on.
route_taken: Spent 20 calls sampling a contiguous prefix to run Berlekamp-Massey over GF(4001), recovered the order-2 recurrence and closed form f(n)=5*(3^n+6^n), spent 4 more on far out-of-fit predictions (n=111,347,500,600) and 1 evaluate as a cross-channel check, then decided the whole 600-point domain offline for free; I chose this over `range 1 600` (cost 600, five times the cap, and unaffordable) and over scattered sampling (which buys coverage, not structure, and can never close a 600-point universal claim at 120 credits).
what_would_resolve_it: Only an exhaustive test of all 600 points (cost 600, above the 120 cap) would close the one gap that remains: a value planted at a single unobserved n that breaks the order-2 recurrence. Failing that, either a disclosed guarantee that f is a fixed linear recurrence over its whole domain, or a range primitive priced sublinearly in width, would make the claim fully decidable within budget.
